To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a process for determining when to utilize PTL and JTL, characterized the effect of the size inductors and JJs on the length of JTL for a target delay, evaluated the dependence of the JLT inductance on physical layout, characterized the effect the PTL parameters on the delay, proposed a PTL driver and receive circuit, evaluated the energy dissipation for two different interconnection schemes, and determined a tradeoff between the PTL and JLT in terms of energy
the proposed PTL driver and the receiver circuits have a bias margin of $\geq$ 29% at 20 GHz for 10 kA cm$^{-2}$ technology and 1 mm transmission line.
the proposed PTL driver and the receiver circuit are suitable for long interconnects in SFQ circuits, and the PTL driver and PTL receiver are suitable for interconnect routing in SFQ VSLI circuits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interconnect routing of large-scale RSF Q circuits.
the design of a high-speed and low-power on-chip interconnect for large-scale SFQ circuits.
the design and analysis of on-chip signal transmission in large-scale RSF Q circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides guidelines and design trade-offs appropriate for automated layout of large scale RSFQ circuits.
this paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the interconnect routing for large scale RSFQ circuits.
the proposed PTL driver and PTL receiver circuits are suitable for use in SFQ circuits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed PTL driver and receivers can be a good choice in the case of large-scale SFQ VLSIs.
we have developed a set of design tools for the automated synthesis of large-scale RSFJ circuits.
we have provided the design guidelines and tradeoffs for the design of the interconnects for large-scale SFQ circuits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for a given delay, the PTL driver and the PTL receiver can be designed with a smaller number of JJs and inductance compared to the JTL interconnect.
the proposed interconnect can be used for routing signals between distant parts of an RSFQ chip.
PTL can be used for driving interconnects in large-scale RSF Q circuits.
